ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Your win rate doesn't tell you if you're profitable.
Units do.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The misconception:
'I'm 60% this month, I must be up.'
Not necessarily. Bet -200 favorites all month at 60% and you're losing money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Win rate ignores the odds you took.
Units account for both side: how often you win AND what you were paid.
A 54% bettor at +110 average beats a 60% bettor at -160 average. Every time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example:
10 bets at -160, 6 wins: stake 10u, return 9.75u. Net: -0.25u.
10 bets at +110, 5 wins: stake 10u, return 10.5u. Net: +0.5u.
Lower win rate. More profit.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
SmarterPicks targets 53 to 58% win rate at positive average odds.
YTD: 54.5%, +37.1u, 9.3% ROI across 435 logged bets.
That's what units actually measure.
